name: Name
title: Waking the Dead: Part 3
body: By Aeryn Rudel

name: Name
title: Waking the Dead: \nWhat Has Gone Before

name: Name
body: In Waking the Dead: "Part One—Ghost of a Chance," the warcaster Aiakos delivers Wraithbinder Nekane to the shores of western Immoren to scout places of power that might serve Dominarch Deneghra’s plans. Nekane first investigates the power of an ancient ruin, Nine Stone, to see if its power might serve to build the Well of Annihilation, an ancient Cryxian design believed to be powerful enough to pull a god from Urcaen. But Nine Stone proves to be far too powerful to control, so Nekane and her forces move on to meet with the Orgoth warlord Sabbreth, who suffers under the possession of the artifact the Lash of Horva, and bring these allies up to date regarding Deneghra’s plan. Sabbreth has doubts that Nine Stone is too powerful to control, but she concedes that Nekane, under Deneghra’s command, must know better and offers Orgoth reinforcements to provide support as Nekane continues her scouting mission for other places of power. But recalling Deneghra’s warning that the Orgoth are not long-term allies and are likely to seek domination over Cryx, Nekane rejects Sabbreth’s offer and departs to continue her mission.

name: Name
body: In Waking the Dead: "Part Two—Spirits of the Deep," Swift Sergeant Dana Thorne of Cygnar arrives at Nine Stone in search of evidence of a Cryxian incursion while farther inland, the ones they seek, led by Wraithbinder Nekane, approach their next destination: Dagger Deep, ruins located in an abandoned Rhulic mine…that turns out not to be abandoned after all. Nekane and her forces decimate the Rhulfolk who try to defend the mine before descending into its depths. There, they find evidence that the Rhulfolk had previously battled and lost to cephalyx, a race of subterranean humanoids that used bioengineered to alter themselves into underground horrors. When Nekane and her forces reach the dark ruins of Dagger Deep in a massive cavern far below, the remnants of the cephalyx hive await them on the edge of a vast charnel pit, filled with the corpses the cephalyx have acquired over time. Yet they are no match for the Cryxians, who destroy them, though at a great cost to their own forces. Nekane is not concerned, however—she recognizes that so many corpses in one place, though not good enough to serve as a place to construct their Well of Annihilation or even a necrofactorium, will give her and her master necrotech the resources they need to build a horrifying Cryxian concept: a colossal called a hellraker.

name: Name
body:
Nearly a week had passed since Swift Sergeant Dana Thorne had left the ruins of Nine Stone in pursuit of the Cryxian incursion. The trail, though faint, had wound its way into the Wyrmwall Mountains, drawing Dana and her troop of rangers through river valleys that held little but bare rock or across ground scoured clean by the ebb and flow of the Banwick. Still, there were signs: the lingering stink of necrotite, the sloughed, rotting skin from a Cryxian thrall, and a single track—a massive, clawed thing that could only belong to a helljack of some kind.
The trail had now ended at the mouth of a Rhulic mine, the gaping aperture leading down into impenetrable darkness. The Cryxians had not been so careful here, and the evidence of a battle was as obvious to Dana as was the sun in the sky. Blood had soaked the ground in various places, leaving the dirt a dry reddish hue. Elsewhere, other fluids, oil and hydraulics, stained the ground black.
There were no bodies or wreckage, though it was easy enough to follow the smears and drips that led to the mine. Clearly, what remained after the battle had been dragged or carried down into the dark.

name: Name
body:
"Orders?" Corporal Gendry asked after he and the rest of the rangers had secured the area.
"Follow me," Dana said and led her corporal to the mine entrance. She pointed at a large patch of dried blood. "What do you see?"
Gendry considered her question for a moment, then, "They piled the bodies here."
"Right, and then?"
Gendry stepped deeper into the darkness. "They came back to get them." He crouched and ran his hands over the ground. "Multiple trails. Multiple trips."
Dana nodded. "And why does Cryx need bodies and wrecked machinery?"
"They’re building something."
"Right again. Could be more thralls. Could be more helljacks. Could be something worse."
"Do we follow?" Gendry asked and failed to suppress a shudder. Dana didn’t blame him; whatever they were up against down there had made short work of ten storm legionnaires and Morrow knew how many Rhulfolk.
"No, " Dana replied. "If we go marching into the dark after them, we’ll be blind and outgunned. Just more meat for their grinder."
"Then what?"

name: Name
body:
"We need reinforcements."
***
It took Dana and her rangers a full day to reach Fort Whiterock, a dilapidated stone fortress so weathered that it appeared to be growing out of the mountainside. The edifice bore the sunburst sigil of Morrow, from which House Sunbright, one of the most pious noble families in Cygnar, had taken its own sigil. The god’s mark was faint and eroded, like the fort it adorned, but seeing it gave Dana a spark of hope. If Morrow’s light could find its way here, even in these desolate mountains, then perhaps it would shine on her fortunes as well.
Whiterock was the only sizeable military presences within the upper Wyrmwalls, and it was garrisoned by the former Duke Sunbright’s Yeoman, a pseudo-religious order of rangers renowned for their piety, woodcraft, and skill at arms. Duke Mordrin Sunbright had been a friend to the CRS, but ill health and advanced age had claimed him in 614 AR. His heir, Morgan Sunbright, was largely unknown to Dana, but she hoped the young duke had continued in his father’s footsteps.

name: Name
body:
After explaining her business to the soldiers at the gate, she and Gendry were shown into the fort proper and ultimately into the duke’s solar. The great room was well appointed, and its high, barred embrasures looked out over the mountains and the Banwick River far below.
The duke appeared to be in his mid-twenties with dark hair and a face that was sturdy and proud, if not quite handsome. He wore ornate white armor with the sunburst sigil of his family on his right pauldron and the mark of Morrow emblazoned on his breastplate. Dana recognized the young duke’s panoply: it was the holy plate of a precursor knight, an order of warriors dedicated to Morrow.
The duke stood beside a large table, a faded map spread across its broad stone surface. The rest of the duke’s knightly regalia—a visorless helm and a heavy mace—rested atop the map. He turned as they entered and regarded Dana and Gendry with a gaze both cool and appraising.
"Your Grace," Dana said and bowed. Gendry follow suit.
"You’re chasing Cryxians, are you?" Duke  Sunbright said, his voice a commanding baritone.

name: Name
body:
"We are," Dana replied. "How did you know?"
Duke Sunbright smiled. "Colonel Kraye is a thorough man and an old friend of my family. He thought you might come to me for help and sent word of your mission weeks ago."
"He was right, Your Grace, as are you." Dana approached the table. "We are hunting Cryxians, and we do need your help."
Duke Sunbright moved his helm and mace aside and gestured at the map, which was a detailed rendering of the area around Fort Whiterock. "Then show me where you lost their trail."
"Less lost and more wasn’t foolish enough to follow, Your Grace," Dana said and quickly found the dwarven mine on the map. "They went underground here."
"I don’t blame you for not following. There have been evil rumors about that mine since before my father." The duke put a finger on the map and ran it east to a point without name or label. "Not many know this, but there is a second entrance to the mine. Here."
"Sheer mountain peaks on three sides," Dana noted. "It’s a canyon. Only one way out."

name: Name
body:
"Morrow provides," Duke Sunbright said.
"Your Grace, I do not have sufficient strength to ambush the Cryxians if they emerge here," Dana said. "But . . ."
The duke cut her off. "But I have a hundred Sunbright Yeoman who would dearly love a chance to prove their worth and devotion in battle against such an abominable foe.
He lowered his voice. "It is no secret that the light of my house has waned, Sergeant. It shames me. Some even call my home Castle Forgotten."
Dana smiled at him. "Then, Your Grace, it is high time you were remembered."

name: Name
body:
Wraithbinder Nekane marveled at how much Chatterbane had accomplished in just a few short weeks. The site where they’d slaughtered the cephalyx had been transformed into a functioning necrofactorium, complete with a necrotite-processing depot and a bonejack ossuary, a combination of mechanika workshop and abattoir. Further, the immense skeleton of the hellraker had begun to take shape. It was little more than a framework, but the outline of the great dire machine was clearly visible, and it filled Nekane with awe and pride.
Using the raw materials from the corpses of cephalyx and Rhulfolk as well as the wreckage of their machines, Chatterbane had also bolstered Nekane’s dwindling strike force with a pair of Raptor bonejacks. He now brought the vulpine light warjacks to her for inspection.
"I’ve fitted this one"—Chatterbane tapped the tusked, skull-like head of one of the Raptors—"with reinforced armor plates and a death ripper maw. It will hold its own, even against larger, better-armed foes."

name: Name
body:
"And the other?" Nekane nodded at the second Raptor. A short cannon projected from its bony jaws and a dome-like device pulsing with Cryxlight was affixed to its back.
"Ah, yes," Chatterbane said with a bony grin. "It is fitted with a venom blaster—very effective against soft targets—and I managed to scrape together enough components for an arc node."
Nekane was impressed. An arc node would allow her to channel her spells through the bonejack, doubling or even tripling the reach of her arcane power. "Well done."
She turned her gaze to the hellraker. "Tell me of the colossal."
Chatterbane sighed and fluttered his appendages like an irritated spider. "I have scoured the cephalyx hive and the dwarven mine for every scrap. There simply isn’t enough. I need more raw materials."
Nekane had feared as much. She knew the small necrofactorium they’d built would be insufficient to create the colossal helljack, but it had given them a much-needed respite and allowed them to rebuild their forces to some extent. But now it was time to move on. The next possible location for the necropolis and the Well of Annihilation was the site of an ancient massacre of Morrowan priests called the Vicarate Slaughter. It had to be explored.

name: Name
body: "The mission demands we move." Nekane glanced over at the massive form of the hellraker. "But I will not completely abandon what we’ve built here." Chatterbane looked relieved—it seemed he would not give up his masterpiece lightly. "What are your orders?" "You will remain here while I scout ahead. If there is an exit to the hive, one large enough to move an army through, I must find it." "An army?" Chatterbane said. "The one you will build for me when I secure more materials for you. These mountains are not uninhabited." "I have no further need of flesh," Chatterbane said. "I have all the organics I can use and more. I need steel, iron, machinery." "I am well aware of your needs," Nekane said, irritated by the necrotech’s lecturing tone. "When they are met, how long before the hellraker is complete?" "If I have everything?" Chatterbane scratched his chin with the saw-bladed tip of one spindly limb. "Two months.’ "I will hold you to that. I’ll take Hades, one of the Raptors, and the Furies, and I will leave you the rest of the thralls for menial tasks and the second Raptor for protection."

name: Name
body: "You might leave Hades if you want me properly protected," Chatterbane said. Nekane grinned. "Come now, Chatterbane. A little fear is an excellent motivator, and you have much to do." *** The passageways of the cephalyx hive continued into the mountain for many miles, though signs of disuse became more apparent the deeper Nekane traveled. She surmised the hive must have been larger and more active at some point, and she considered herself fortunate that it was considerably diminished by the time she was forced into conflict with its inhabitants. The glowing furnaces of Hades and the Raptor lighted her way through the labyrinth, but she frequently sent the Furies ahead to scout, their tripartite voices filling the empty warren of tunnels with feral whispers. In many places, the passageways narrowed considerably, tight enough that Hades could not pass through, forcing Nekane to find another way around. Though little more than an inconvenience for a small party, these constricted tunnels guaranteed a sizeable force, such as an army, would struggle to navigate the hive.

name: Name
body: A day passed, then another, and the hive gave way to more conventional passages. The Rhulfolk had dug their mine from both sides of the mountain, but, here, too, there was a keen sense of abandonment. The machinery she passed was in poor repair, pitted with rust, and entirely unsuitable for Chatterbane’s needs. It seemed both the hive and the mine would not serve any of her purposes. On the third day of traveling through empty darkness, the Furies returned from a scouting mission, their ghostly voices eager and excited. "The mountain opens," said Dogreth. "We smell life on the air," added Valek. "But the sun shines," finished Anathan, fear and disgust staining her sibilant voice. Though it didn’t affect their abilities, the wraiths hated the sun and avoided it when they could. Nekane couldn’t indulge their preference for darkness now, however. She was momentarily concerned that the Furies had detected a living presence, but to her knowledge, there was no enemy military presence on this side of the mountain. The life the wraiths detected might be a village or settlement where she could find some of the resources she needed. Exposing herself during the daylight hours was risky, but after so long underground, she needed to get her bearings and perhaps ascertain how close she was to the site of the Vicarate Slaughter, their next stop.

name: Name
body:
"We press ahead."
Nekane turned the furnaces on both her warjacks to full stoke, choking the narrow passages with greasy, black smoke. Light appeared ahead. It grew steadily brighter. The exit to the mine was wide and clear, and the sunlight streamed in, banishing the gloom and prompting an angry hiss from the Furies.
"To me," Nekane ordered, and the three wraiths reluctantly surrounded her, a shield of spectral power.
Nekane summoned Hades and the Raptor to her side as well, then stepped out of darkness for the first time in weeks. She winced, turned her head to the side, and walked out into the bright sun.
It was a mistake.
The shriek of an electrical discharge filled the air, and the stench of ozone struck Nekane’s nose seconds before the cliff face above the mine entrance exploded in a geyser of rock and dirt.
Nekane was thrown forward by the blast and fell to her knees. She looked up and saw she’d been flung into a small mountain canyon with a sluggish stream running along the rocky floor. Sheer cliffs rose on three sides, impassable, and the only exit out of the canyon was to the east, where a dozen men and women armed with rifles stood beside a pair of light warjacks armed with voltaic blades and storm thrower cannons. It was one of the latter weapons that had brought the hillside above the mine crashing down, sealing off Nekane’s only other avenue of escape.

name: Name
body:
The enemy rifles opened up, and bullets sparked off Nekane’s power field. She sprang to her feet and ducked behind Hades. More bullets bounced off the helljack’s armored hull or passed harmlessly through the incorporeal bodies of the Furies.
Nekane took quick stock of her situation. The enemy forces were not overwhelming, but she could still recognize it as a scouting party. If she stood and fought, she’d be pinned in when enemy reinforcements arrived and ultimately annihilated her.

name: Name
body:
"Return to Chatterbane," Nekane shouted at the Furies. The incorporeal spirits could pass through the rubble blocking the mine entrance. "Tell him what has happened and to remain where he is until I contact him."
Bullets and the screeching discharge of storm cannons echoed through the valley, and Nekane felt Hades’ sudden rage as a bolt of galvanic energy struck his hull. The helljack wanted to charge into melee, but Nekane held him in check.
"Go!" Nekane commanded, and the Furies melted into the stony debris and disappeared.
She turned her attention to her enemies and urged Hades and the Raptor into a charge while she ran behind them, letting them outdistance her just to the point where she could still control their actions directly.
She called forth her magic and cast a spell on Hades. The helljack’s black iron form shimmered, then blinked forward thirty yards, appearing directly in front of one of the enemy warjacks. The helljack’s death claw scythed out, ripping through the Cygnaran warjack’s hull, tearing one of its arms completely from its body.

name: Name
body:
The Cygnaran troops were lightly armed and armored rangers, though they all bore a curious sunburst on their white leather breastplates. It reminded her of the sigil of the human god Morrow, and she repressed a shudder. Her mission was to seek out a site with enough blasphemous power to pull a god from Urcaen, perhaps Morrow himself, in order that Sabbreth could destroy him. The appearance of his sigil and followers here, now, was a grim, unwelcome omen.
The rangers poured rifle fire into the Raptor. They clearly knew a softer target when they saw one. The ghostly impacts of each bullet flowed back through Nekane’s connection with the bonejack pinpricks across her body, but it hadn’t suffered any debilitating harm yet. The Raptor scuttled to within a few yards of the ranked Cygnaran troops, opened its bony jaws wide, and sprayed a thick, caustic spume over the enemy.
Screams of horror and pain rose above the gunfire followed by the shattering sounds of steel on steel as the flesh of Nekane’s enemies dissolved and liquified.

name: Name
body: Very effective against soft targets, Nekane thought with a feral grin. Hades had all but dismantled the first warjack, but instead of compelling the helljack to attack the second enemy machine, Nekane urged the ’jack to seize its current foe, hoist it up, and hurl it. Three tons of half-wrecked warjack sailed through the air and smashed into the second enemy machine, knocking it to the ground and pinning it beneath its ruined compatriot. With both their warjacks momentarily disabled, the Cygnaran troops reeled back, and Nekane saw a chance to flee. She pulled Hades and the Raptor to her side and forced them into a desperate, loping run. They quickly left the enemy behind save for a handful of harrying rifle shots. As she ran, Nekane checked the status of her warjacks. Both were damaged but still fully functional. She’d been fortunate. But a black plumes of smoke drifted over the canyon walls ahead—the burning bloom of a warjack furnace—and she knew she could not trust to luck any longer.

name: Name
body:
***
The canyon seemed endless, the mountains loomed overhead, and Nekane ran with her breath hammering from her lungs, her heart pounding beneath the weight of her armor. Hades and the Raptor kept pace, but they were rapidly burning necrotite, and soon she would be forced to slow down or not have sufficient fuel for battle.
Ahead, smoke rose in a thin stream, a clear sign of the enemy, but there was no other direction for her to go. She clung to one scant hope of escape: She was currently at a high elevation, above the tree line, but if she reached the thick forests that dominated the lower climes of the Wyrmwalls, she could hide long enough for night to fall. Then, under cover of darkness, she might make her way back to Chatterbane and the Necrofactorium.
She pushed on, hoping she could battle through any further resistance she encountered. As the canyon wove sharply to the east, the stream at its center deepening, that hope was suddenly dashed.
A wall of Cygnaran troops stood in her path, rangers clad in white leather, their rifles leveled. In their center stood a singular figure, a robust human man clad in archaic armor, snow white, Morrow’s sigil marked out in yellow on his breastplate. He gripped a heavy steel mace in one hand and a sturdy shield in the other. Beside him stood a relic of bygone days, a towering warjack spewing black smoke into the air from two heavy, brass-wreathed stacks. The Ironclad, though decades old, appeared more than serviceable, and the quake hammer it held in its left hand gleamed with dull, ugly menace.

name: Name
body: The white-armored knight stepped forward and raised his mace. "I am Duke Morgan Sunbright, and in the name of Queen Marjorie Raelthorne, I demand you lay down your arms, deactivate your abominable machines, and surrender." The grim realization she would likely die here settled over Nekane. The certainty of it granted her a kind of serenity. She was Cryxian and Iosan, and if her twin heritages had taught her anything, it was that there were far worse things than death. She tapped into Hades’ cortex, let the helljack’s unbridled rage flow into her, suffusing her with confidence and eagerness for battle. Then she answered her enemy’s challenge. "I am Wraithbinder Nekane," she called out. "Let me pass or you will die, and when you do, I promise you will not go to your god. You will be extinguished, utterly, mind and soul." The knight shook his head, turned back toward his troops, and instantly the world exploded into chaos. Sixty rifles fired simultaneously, shredding the air with bullets. Nekane, again, ducked behind Hades. The helljack’s armored hull would shield her from light arms, though not indefinitely. Even a machine as mighty as Hades could be brought down with sustained fire. Her bonejack, however, stood no chance. The phantom sting of dozens of rifle slugs bloomed across her body, and then came the wrenching pain as they smashed apart the Raptor’s internal components. The bonejack’s presence disappeared from her mind like an unremembered dream.

name: Name
body:
Nekane knew Hades would not withstand another volley, and if she were going to take any of her enemies with her, she would need to get close. Thirty yards separated her and the front line of rangers. She pushed Hades forward, still using the helljack as cover, and aimed its soul cannon at the enemy line. The cannon discharged, sending a gout of green fire into her foes. Half a dozen rangers were killed, and their souls, streams of howling spectral energy, flowed into Hades, filling the helljack with new power.
The horror of her attack rocked the enemy back on their heels for a moment, and Nekane seized that opportunity and used the stolen soul energy to teleport Hades within a few yards of the enemy, on the other end of the canyon from the Ironclad.
Hades did not need any urging to fall upon the rangers. It barreled into their midst, its death claw scything out, reducing while-clad rangers to dismembered corpses. With each death, Hades drank souls and teleported again. Its great iron form shimmered from point to point, leaving more corpses behind with each jump.

name: Name
body:
Nekane raced toward the right flank of the enemy line. Bullets sparked from her power field or deflected from her armor, but she reached her destination unscathed. In close quarters, the rangers’ rifles were cumbersome—the Cygnarans were forced to use their knives. They were no match for her in the brutal press of melee, and Nekane’s hell spike reaped blood and souls, turning her body ghostly and insubstantial after each kill, further confounding the blades of her enemies.
For a moment, she lost herself in the simple delight of combat, but she was dragged back to the dire truth of her situation as sudden, catastrophic damage to Hades roared through their connection. The Ironclad had engaged her helljack, and to prevent Hades from teleporting away, it gripped the helljack’s hull with one massive fist.
Hades tore at the Ironclad’s body, ripping away armor plates, but it wasn’t enough. The Cygnaran warjack brought its quake hammer down like a descending meteor, smashing Hades right arm to useless wreckage.

name: Name
body:
Nekane cried out as the ghostly pains of the helljack’s injuries flowed back to her. She saw Duke Sunbright close with Hades as well and soon felt the dread caress of his blessed mace on the helljack’s hull.
The searing bite of an enemy knife pulled Nekane back to more immediate surroundings and concerns. One of the rangers, a steel-haired veteran clad in more traditional blue-and-brown ranger garb had plunged his knife into her side. Nekane jerked back, ripping the weapon from her enemy’s hand, then lunged forward, punching her hell spike into his chest. He gasped. His mouth stretched open in a silent, blood-flecked scream as she tore his soul from his flesh, using it to become incorporeal again.
Strangely, she found herself in a lull in the battle. Most of the rangers had been drawn toward the battle between Hades and the Ironclad, likely to protect their leader. Nekane saw two opportunities. She could take control of Hades and rip Duke Sunbright to bloody tatters before she herself was overwhelmed and killed. It would mean her own demise, but the option appealed. She had promised the Morrowan death, and she was not one to make such oaths idly. But she could see the end of the canyon only a short distance away and beyond it, the tree line and possible sanctuary.

name: Name
body:
The choice was simple. The mission above all.
She slashed free of the few remaining rangers around her, taking two more wounds for her trouble. Then she was past the melee and running, blood sluicing down her side, the pain pushing her on.
She felt the impact of the Ironclad’s quake hammer again, a sharp pain in her ribs as the brutal weapon staved in Hades’ hull. Mercifully, the helljack dwindled in her mind as she neared the edge of her control radius. She reached the trees, and Hades’ mighty presence slipped away.

name: Name
body:
Nekane woke to darkness and pain. The first was a blessing; the latter, a cold reminder of loss and failure. She’d concealed herself beneath the tangled roots of a great pine tree and waited for night to fall. Her enemies had searched the area, and rangers had passed within a few feet of her hiding spot, but they hadn’t found her.
Now, with the cover of night, she could risk moving. She crawled out of her refuge, every joint aching, her wounds sending spikes of agony through her body, but she found the strength to stand. To further conceal her presence, she’d shut down her armor’s furnace, and the weight of it was monstrous on her shoulders and back. She switched it on, and as the mechanika powered up, it took up the weight, drawing from her an audible sigh of relief.
Nekane glanced around. She had little notion of which direction she should travel. In her desperate flight to escape the Cygnarans, she’d failed to take note of her path and was now hopelessly lost.
She stood, silent, and tried to get her bearings. She felt a cold wind blowing from the west, heard the distant cry of night bird from the east, and, then, to the south, something pulled at her. Not a physical sensation. Whatever this was tugged at her mind the way a helljack’s presence filled her consciousness. It was power she felt. Distant but unmistakable.

name: Name
body:
She turned south and began to walk, the slope of the mountainside adding speed to her gait. That sensation of power grew and took on new dimension. She was keenly attuned to death, especially violent death, and the stain it left behind. What drew her on fairly hummed with the strength of horror and the potency of murder. Excitement washed away her weariness, and she fought the urge to run, to race toward the source of such exquisite torment.
She walked for hours, a death-hungry moth drawn to the balefire of pain, but when she reached the source, there were no ruins, no crumbling remnants of ancient Morrdh or the more recent edifices of the Orgoth. There was only a circle of bare earth, a wide clearing within the depths of a mountain forest. Nothing grew upon the scorched heath, and the soil itself was ashy and crumbling, devoid of life and enriched with death.
Nekane knelt, put her hand on the savaged earth, and grinned. This was it. Everything she’d been looking for. Here she could build a necropolis. Here she could wrest from the ground the Well of Annihilation.

name: Name
body:
She had found the site of the Vicarate Slaughter, or, more correctly, it had found her. The Orgoth had massacred hundreds of Morrowan priests centuries ago in a brutal but ultimately futile attempt to purge those gifted with magic. They had taken the bodies of those priests and buried them here in a communal grave. The priests’ savage end and the cruel anonymity of their murder had coalesced into something far stronger than sites of more celebrated atrocities.
Sudden motion in the trees broke Nekane’s revery and brought her instantly to her feet, her hell spike extending from her arm.
"Who are you?" she said. "Come forth."
A tall, ill-shaped form stepped from the pooled shadows beneath the trees and shambled toward her. There was something oddly familiar about it. When the feeble light of Caen’s moons splashed upon the misshapen figure, Nekane suddenly recognized it.
Discerptor Eviscerus had once been mortal, as had been most who served the Nightmare Empire, but nearly every trace of the organic creature he’d been had withered and rotted away over the centuries. What was left was a hunched monstrosity of steel, iron, and bronze, with four crab-like appendages fitted with vise-like claws for walking or grasping plus two smaller arms ending in taloned hands for finer manipulations. The discerptor’s head was cowled and hung low on his hunched frame. All Nekane could see of his face was a blank oval of bone, a skull weathered almost smooth by the incalculable passage of years.

name: Name
body:
Nekane was only vaguely familiar with Eviscerus. As discerptor, his role in the Necrofactorium was to scavenge on the mainland for new technologies and ancient secrets. He’d apparently been at this task for over six centuries, and few in the Necrofactorium had ever encountered him. There were, of course, rumors about the venerable Eviscerus—that his mind had become scattered, his actions and motives erratic. He was also reputed to have curious prescience for being in the right place at the right time. He somehow knew when and where an ancient tomb might open and disgorge its secrets or, perhaps, when a member of the Necrofactorium required aid.
Despite his bizarre reputation, he was nominally an ally. Possibly a powerful one.
"Discerptor—" Nekane began, but Eviscerus cut her off.
"The Vicarate Slaughter occurred in 69 AR," he said in a low rasp, and then his voice changed, became fuller, more confident. "No, no, no. It was closer to 68 AR after the wizard Jerdon Tauthis was identified by the . . . by the . . ." he trailed off, his voice fading into almost inaudible mumbling.

name: Name
body: Nekane realized the discerptor was not speaking to her. It sounded more as if he were having a conversation with himself. "Discerptor," Nekane tried again, "I require your assistance." "Assistance?" Eviscerus said. "Assistance. The word is from the old Morrdhish for aid, accustus." His voice had taken on the lecturer’s tone again. "I am sent by Dominarch Deneghra," Nekane said. "I am on a mission of utmost importance to the Necrofactorium. Do you understand?" The discerptor turned his face up to her. The featureless skull betrayed nothing. "Who are you?" His voice took on a third dimension, more present, a seeming moment of clarity. Nekane seized on it. "I am Wraithbinder Nekane. I am sent by Dominarch Deneghra to find a site suitable for a Necropolis, with enough power to honor our pact with the Orgoth—" "No!" Eviscerus howled and surged forward, his hands scrabbling at Nekane’s face. She nearly shot him with her rune thrower as he pressed his clawed fingers to her lips. "We do not say it. We do not breath it. Do not. Do not. DO NOT."

name: Name
body:
Nekane gently pushed the discerptor’s hands away from her face. She was dealing with a creature whose mind had fractured, but she still required his help. She knew Eviscerus’ past was somehow tangled up in the first Orgoth invasion, and it was clear the discerptor was buried under trauma related to that event, trauma that had likely grown huge and cancerous over his long years.
"Can you help me?" Nekane breathed. "I am alone. I need helljacks, thralls, anything you can provide."
"Help you?"
"I need to secure this site for a Necropolis, but I lack the strength to do so. We are allies. We both serve the Necrofactorium."
"Serve. Allies. Help," Eviscerus said as if he had never heard these words before. "Helljacks. Thralls."
"Yes. Do you understand?"
Eviscerus suddenly whirled around and scuttled toward the trees. Nekane watched him go, unsure what to do, but once the discerptor reached the tree line, he turned and motioned her to follow him. With little choice, she did.
***
Nekane followed Eviscerus through the trees. His path was erratic, and sometimes he stopped, muttered to himself before completely changing direction. Finally, with the sky turning steel gray with the coming dawn, they came to massive, moss-covered boulder in a small clearing.

name: Name
body:
Eviscerus stopped and looked back at her. "Discerptor Eviscerus is known to secret much of the technology he finds in caches and to stock them with servitors for later use."
Nekane blinked. It was as if the discerptor were reading a description of himself from a history book, a bizarre kind of derealization. Still, his words brought hope and excitement. "Is there such a cache here?"
Eviscerus moved to the boulder and touched it at various points with the tip of a talon. A low rumbling emanated from beneath the ground—and the huge piece of stone shifted aside, revealing a dark pit some fifteen feet in diameter in the forest floor. Crude steps descended into the earth.
The discerptor disappeared into the yawning aperture. Nekane followed. The smell of dust and death came to her as she descended, but she could see almost nothing. She reached the bottom of the steps and heard the drip of water, felt a chill in the air. The light from her warcaster armor cast enough illumination that she could tell she had entered a cavernous space.

name: Name
body: Necrotic green light suddenly filled the space, shed from floating spheres of bronze and glass. Nekane’s breath caught in her throat. The sheer size of the cache was staggering: a great vault stretching hundreds of feet, every inch covered with artifacts, bits of machinery, and piles of raw materials. But these were only scraps compared to the rest. Dozens of mechanithralls lined the vault walls, inert but fully intact. The ivory gleam of bonejack skulls shone in the gangrenous light, and she spied a pair of helljacks, Slayers, likely a century old. An army of hibernating monsters awaiting her command. "How many caches like this do you have?" Eviscerus turned to her. "Discerptor Eviscerus is rumored to have dozens of secret stockpiles and repositories scattered throughout the Wyrmwall Mountains." Nekane smiled. "And Wraithbinder Nekane will make use of them all."
